message.content: monokl: change the search row columns, as measured by the column-economics study (222 queries, 2,038 rows, o200k tokens; `rank` equals the row index in 2038/2038 rows, 3.8% of tokens; `finalScore` is 9.2% as 6-decimal floats; the top1/top2 score ratio is informative (AUC 0.80; ratio>=1.5 flags 118 queries as clear with 94% precision) but absolute scores are not comparable across queries; nothing in scripts/rg-compare.py or scripts/agent-cost.py reads rank or finalScore). Do: (1) DROP the `rank` column from the search row schema (SEARCH_FIELDS in crates/monokl/src/output/agent.rs and the wire/row type); (2) REPLACE `finalScore` with an integer percent of the top row's score (top row = 100; round to nearest integer, clamp to 0..=100; if the top score is 0 or the row set is empty use a defined fallback and test it); name the column `relevance` (or `scorePct` if michi's field naming rules need camelCase: check the existing naming convention of columns and follow it; state the choice); it aligns with `--min-score` (the cut keeps rows with score >= min_score x top, so relevance < 100*min_score are exactly the cut rows): state this in the docs and make the `--min-score` help text and the paging hints reference it consistently. The internal float score stays in core for the cut and ordering (core result types are not Serialize and have no rendering; the wire shape lives in the output layer). Compute the percent from the same float used for ordering, never from a re-parsed string. Do NOT change any other column, order, or the lean defaults. Delete code and tests made dead (e.g. score formatting). Update every test expectation by recomputing exactly (never loosen), README examples, docs/architecture output docs, the decision-log (next free section number on main; record the measurement, the rejected candidates: lines merge, lineStart+span, short nodeKind, blank repeated files, group by file, null as empty cell, score as 1/2 decimals, drop finalScore outright with reasons from the study: lines merge breaks agent-cost 206->0; grouping reorders 136/222; 1dp makes top1==top2 in 7 queries), and add a changeset: minor with **Breaking:** (the columns `rank` and `finalScore` are gone; `relevance` is new) and **Action:** (parse by header name, not position; to rank-order use row order; `relevance` is a percent of the top row) notes. Cut from origin/main (`git fetch origin && git switch -c feat/lean-columns origin/main`); PRs #113 (lean Rust rows) and the michi 0.10 migration (branch feat/michi-0.10, may not exist yet) touch output/agent.rs: when either lands on main, merge origin/main and keep both. Verify by exit code: `just lint`, `just test` x2, `just rg-compare` (baseline identifiers 59/59, questions 17/18, members 15/16, Rust fd 22/24, held-out 32/33 and 22/22, held-out Rust 35/36, rhf 14/14; answerable 206/222), `just agent-cost` (script must still read rows: its regex needs file,lineStart,lineEnd first), `just changesets`, `just typos`, `just bench`; and re-measure median/p90 bytes and tokens (bytes/3.5 if tiktoken is unavailable) over the 222 queries before/after, expecting about -9% tokens. Git: Conventional Commits; commit messages end with `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AdtWVgDi4y4qCnpfdozb2n`; push; `entire trail link 361 --branch feat/lean-columns --base main` (never trail create / gh pr create / force-push); `gh pr ready`; PR description ends with `https://claude.ai/code/session_01AdtWVgDi4y4qCnpfdozb2n` and shows one real query's output before and after. Owner's rule: if Entire shows a finding on this change, RESOLVE or dismiss it in Entire BEFORE pushing the fix: `entire trail finding resolve <change-ref> <ULID> -m <reason> --project gh/orin-dx`. Isolated worktree; never touch `.claude/settings.json`; network/signing/gh/entire need dangerouslyDisableSandbox. Report <=120 words.

# List available commands
default:
    @just --list

# Install the cargo tools the recipes below use
install-tools:
    cargo install cargo-nextest cargo-llvm-cov cargo-machete cargo-mutants cargo-deny typos-cli zizmor --locked
    rustup component add llvm-tools-preview

# Install the pinned toolchain and the moon-managed git hooks
setup:
    proto install
    moon sync vcs-hooks

# Build the workspace. One `cargo --workspace` invocation, not `moon run :build`: per-crate cargo processes all
# contend for the same target/ lock and serialize.
build:
    cargo build --workspace --locked

build-release:
    cargo build --workspace --release --locked

# Run tests with nextest, plus doctests, which nextest does not run. The default-features pass catches code that only
# builds because --all-features turned something on.
test:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features --locked
    cargo nextest run --workspace --locked
    cargo test --doc --workspace --all-features --locked

# Line coverage; fails below the threshold, which this default owns
coverage threshold="90":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --locked --lcov --output-path lcov.info
    cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only --fail-under-lines "{{ threshold }}"

# Coverage report, opened in the browser
coverage-html:
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --locked --html --open

# Format check, clippy with and without default features, and typos, the same as CI's lint job
lint: typos
    cargo fmt --all --check
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --no-default-features --locked -- -D warnings

# Clippy on the crates moon reports as affected, in one cargo invocation
lint-affected:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    projects=$(moon query projects --affected | jq -r '.projects[].id')
    if [ -z "$projects" ]; then exit 0; fi
    args=()
    for p in $projects; do args+=(-p "$p"); done
    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings

fmt:
    cargo fmt --all

# Documentation build, with warnings (including broken intra-doc links) as errors
doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --all-features --locked
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --locked

# Licenses, advisories, bans and sources
deny:
    cargo deny check

# Unused dependencies
machete:
    cargo machete

typos:
    typos

# Callisto config, package discovery and pending changesets; the same gate as CI's Changesets job
changesets:
    callisto status --check --strict
    callisto release --dry-run --format text

# Record a pending change for the next release, e.g. `just changeset minor "Add the search command"`
changeset bump summary:
    callisto add --package cargo/monokl:{{ bump }} --summary "{{ summary }}"

# Workflow audit for permission, credential and supply-chain issues
zizmor:
    zizmor --offline --strict-collection .

# Fails when a duplicated fact disagrees with its owner, e.g. the Callisto pin in the workflows against .prototools
check-drift:
    scripts/check-drift.sh

# Checks a published release is complete and usable, e.g. `just verify-release 0.4.0`. Needs network and gh.
verify-release version:
    scripts/verify-release.sh {{ version }}

# Score search targeting and output size against ripgrep on pinned public repos. Needs network and `rg`; on demand, not part of `just ci`.
rg-compare *args:
    cargo build --release -q
    python3 -I scripts/rg-compare.py {{ args }}

# Bytes, estimated tokens and turns of one `monokl search` against a fixed rg-only agent policy on the rg-compare questions; deterministic, no model. Report only. Needs network and `rg`; on demand.
agent-cost *args:
    cargo build --release -q
    python3 -I scripts/test_agent_cost.py
    python3 -I scripts/agent-cost.py {{ args }}

# Time and peak memory of `monokl search` against ripgrep on pinned repos and a stress set. Warm cache; needs network and `rg`; on demand.
bench *args:
    cargo build --release -q
    python3 -I scripts/bench.py {{ args }}

# Block span and parent invariants over the harness repositories in target/rg-compare (`just rg-compare` fills it) or the directories in MONOKL_SPAN_CORPUS; skips with a message when neither exists. On demand.
span-invariants:
    cargo test -p monokl --test span_invariants --release -- --ignored --nocapture

# Mutation testing. Slow, so on demand only, not part of `just ci`.
mutants:
    cargo mutants --workspace

# Public API SemVer check against the last published version. Not in `just ci` until a first release exists.
check-api:
    cargo semver-checks check-release

clean:
    moon clean 2>/dev/null || true
    cargo clean

# Run by the moon-managed pre-commit hook
pre-commit:
    cargo fmt --all --check
    typos

# Run by the moon-managed pre-push hook
pre-push: pre-commit lint-affected

# Everything the CI jobs run
ci: lint test doc-check deny machete typos zizmor check-drift changesets coverage

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""What a coding agent pays to answer each rg-compare question with `monokl search` against ripgrep alone. No model, no
3	timing: bytes, estimated tokens and turns, all deterministic for a pinned checkout and a binary.
4	
5	Rows are the rg-compare harness's: sampled identifiers (rg-compare.repos), concept questions and member lookups
6	(rg-compare.questions), on every repository including the held-out and report-only ones. Sets mirror the harness's
7	lines: identifiers, questions, members, rust (fd identifiers, questions and members pooled), held-out questions,
8	held-out members, held-out rust and report-only (the repositories marked `report-only`), plus all.
9	
10	monokl cost. One `monokl search <words> .` with default caps, as `rg-compare.py` runs it. Bytes are the size of its
11	stdout, tokens are ceil(bytes / 3) (the product's own estimate), turns are 1. The row is answerable in one turn when
12	one of the first 3 rows (blocks) is in the expected file, spans the expected declaration's line and shows the
13	declaration's text, so the agent needs no follow-up read. `monokl+read` is the same cost with one more turn for a
14	file read of the expected block when the row is not answerable, so a miss is not counted as free.
15	
16	rg-policy cost. A fixed policy standing in for an agent that only has ripgrep. Every step favors rg:
17	
18	  1. Best term. For an identifier, the identifier. For a question, the word whose `rg -n` output has the fewest
19	     non-test lines (at least one; ties go to the longer word, then alphabetical order), which an agent could only
20	     know by trying every word.
21	  2. Turn 1: `rg -n -S -w <best term>` over the language's source files. Test files are dropped, as monokl drops
22	     them. The agent reads the first 200 lines, each cut to 300 bytes, with no `./` prefix; matches are sorted by path.
23	  3. Turn 2, only when turn 1 matched more than 50 lines: a narrower `rg -n`, read the same way. For an identifier,
24	     the declaration pattern of that identifier. For a question, lines holding the two best words in either order.
25	     A question with fewer than two words that match has no narrower pattern and skips turn 2.
26	  4. Last turn: a file read of the lines of the block that holds the declaration. The extent is monokl's own, from
27	     the first and last line of the rows of `monokl search <symbol>` with the lean cut off (`--min-score 0`, no row
28	     or token cap, `--snippet-lines 0`); the declaration line is found by rg, and ranking plays no part, so the
29	     measurement does not depend on where monokl ranks the answer. For each declaration line the block is the
30	     innermost block holding it (a class does not stand in for its method), and the largest of those counts, so an
31	     implementation is read in place of its overload signatures. Across several expected files the smallest counts.
32	     A declaration with no body, such as Rust's `mod name;`, has no block and is read as its own line; the report
33	     lists them. The extent is monokl's, so a TypeScript block starts at the declaration and a Rust block also holds
34	     the doc comments and attributes above it. An analyzer extent bug would raise or lower the read cost and monokl's
35	     own rows alike. rg is never charged for failing to find the file: the policy always succeeds, and `rg_located`
36	     reports how often the expected file was in the lines the agent actually read. `scripts/test_agent_cost.py`
37	     checks the extents with exact bytes; `just agent-cost` runs it first.
38	
39	Turns are the rg calls plus the read; bytes are the sum of the lines read in each call plus the read. `rg-early`
40	repeats the policy but stops, with no read, as soon as a turn shows the expected declaration's line; it is the cheaper
41	agent that trusts a matching line, and tokens use the same ceil(bytes / 3) as monokl.
42	
43	Report only. A line starting `FAIL` is printed when a set's median monokl bytes exceed its median rg-policy bytes or
44	when its answerable-in-one-turn rate is below 0.8; the exit status stays 0. This is not a model evaluation: it says
45	what each route costs if the agent does what the policy says, not whether a model would find the answer.
46	
47	Repositories are the clones `rg-compare.py` keeps in target/rg-compare, fetched on demand at the pinned shas.
48	"""
49	
50	import argparse
51	import importlib.util
52	import json
53	import math
54	import re
55	import sys
56	from pathlib import Path
57	
58	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
59	# rg-compare.py owns the repositories, questions, declaration patterns and monokl's file rules; load it by path.
60	_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("rg_compare", ROOT / "scripts" / "rg-compare.py")
61	RC = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec)
62	_spec.loader.exec_module(RC)
63	
64	TOP_ROWS = 3
65	FIRST_LINES = 200
66	LINE_CAP = 300
67	NARROW_ABOVE = 50
68	MIN_ONE_TURN = 0.8
69	ROW = re.compile(r"^  ([^,\n]+),(\d+),(\d+),")
70	BARE = str.maketrans("", "", '"\\')
71	TOOLS = ("monokl", "monokl+read", "rg-policy", "rg-early")
72	SETS = ("identifiers", "questions", "members", "rust", "held-out questions", "held-out members", "held-out rust",
73	        "report-only", "all")
74	
75	
76	def tokens(byte_count):
77	    return math.ceil(byte_count / 3)
78	
79	
80	def percentile(values, share):
81	    """Nearest rank: the smallest value with at least `share` of the values at or below it."""
82	    ordered = sorted(values)
83	    return ordered[max(math.ceil(share * len(ordered)) - 1, 0)]
84	
85	
86	def median(values):
87	    ordered = sorted(values)
88	    mid = len(ordered) // 2
89	    return ordered[mid] if len(ordered) % 2 else (ordered[mid - 1] + ordered[mid]) / 2
90

122	    """(line number, text) of every declaration of `symbol` in `file`, as rg finds them."""

132	def monokl_spans(binary, symbol, path, file):
133	    """(first line, last line) of every block monokl returns for `file` when it searches `symbol` with the lean cut
134	    off (no score floor, no row cap, no token cap). Only extents are read: the declaration is found by rg, and monokl's

136	    out = RC.run([binary, "search", symbol, ".", "--min-score", "0", "--max-results", "1000000", "--max-tokens",

138	    rows = [(m.group(1).removeprefix("./"), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3)))

144	    """(first line, last line) of the block that is the declaration: for each declaration line, the innermost block

146	    implementation is read in place of its overload signatures. None when no block holds any declaration line."""
147	    innermost = set()

150	        if holding:

183	    """Runs monokl once; returns (bytes, answerable in the first rows, how many rows were printed)."""

196	def rg_policy(path, lang, words, identifier, expected, cache, read):
197	    """Simulates the rg-only agent; returns its turns, bytes, whether the expected file was read, and the early-stop

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""What a coding agent pays to answer each rg-compare question with `monokl search` against ripgrep alone. No model, no
timing: bytes, estimated tokens and turns, all deterministic for a pinned checkout and a binary.

Rows are the rg-compare harness's: sampled identifiers (rg-compare.repos), concept questions and member lookups
(rg-compare.questions), on every repository including the held-out and report-only ones. Sets mirror the harness's
lines: identifiers, questions, members, rust (fd identifiers, questions and members pooled), held-out questions,
held-out members, held-out rust and report-only (the repositories marked `report-only`), plus all.

monokl cost. One `monokl search <words> .` with default caps, as `rg-compare.py` runs it. Bytes are the size of its
stdout, tokens are ceil(bytes / 3) (the product's own estimate), turns are 1. The row is answerable in one turn when
one of the first 3 rows (blocks) is in the expected file, spans the expected declaration's line and shows the
declaration's text, so the agent needs no follow-up read. `monokl+read` is the same cost with one more turn for a
file read of the expected block when the row is not answerable, so a miss is not counted as free.

rg-policy cost. A fixed policy standing in for an agent that only has ripgrep. Every step favors rg:

  1. Best term. For an identifier, the identifier. For a question, the word whose `rg -n` output has the fewest
     non-test lines (at least one; ties go to the longer word, then alphabetical order), which an agent could only
     know by trying every word.
  2. Turn 1: `rg -n -S -w <best term>` over the language's source files. Test files are dropped, as monokl drops
     them. The agent reads the first 200 lines, each cut to 300 bytes, with no `./` prefix; matches are sorted by path.
  3. Turn 2, only when turn 1 matched more than 50 lines: a narrower `rg -n`, read the same way. For an identifier,
     the declaration pattern of that identifier. For a question, lines holding the two best words in either order.
     A question with fewer than two words that match has no narrower pattern and skips turn 2.
  4. Last turn: a file read of the lines of the block that holds the declaration. The extent is monokl's own, from
     the first and last line of the rows of `monokl search <symbol>` with the lean cut off (`--min-score 0`, no row
     or token cap, `--snippet-lines 0`); the declaration line is found by rg, and ranking plays no part, so the
     measurement does not depend on where monokl ranks the answer. For each declaration line the block is the
     innermost block holding it (a class does not stand in for its method), and the largest of those counts, so an
     implementation is read in place of its overload signatures. Across several expected files the smallest counts.
     A declaration with no body, such as Rust's `mod name;`, has no block and is read as its own line; the report
     lists them. The extent is monokl's, so a TypeScript block starts at the declaration and a Rust block also holds
     the doc comments and attributes above it. An analyzer extent bug would raise or lower the read cost and monokl's
     own rows alike. rg is never charged for failing to find the file: the policy always succeeds, and `rg_located`
     reports how often the expected file was in the lines the agent actually read. `scripts/test_agent_cost.py`
     checks the extents with exact bytes; `just agent-cost` runs it first.

Turns are the rg calls plus the read; bytes are the sum of the lines read in each call plus the read. `rg-early`
repeats the policy but stops, with no read, as soon as a turn shows the expected declaration's line; it is the cheaper
agent that trusts a matching line, and tokens use the same ceil(bytes / 3) as monokl.

Report only. A line starting `FAIL` is printed when a set's median monokl bytes exceed its median rg-policy bytes or
when its answerable-in-one-turn rate is below 0.8; the exit status stays 0. This is not a model evaluation: it says
what each route costs if the agent does what the policy says, not whether a model would find the answer.

Repositories are the clones `rg-compare.py` keeps in target/rg-compare, fetched on demand at the pinned shas.
"""

import argparse
import importlib.util
import json
import math
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
# rg-compare.py owns the repositories, questions, declaration patterns and monokl's file rules; load it by path.
_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("rg_compare", ROOT / "scripts" / "rg-compare.py")
RC = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec)
_spec.loader.exec_module(RC)

TOP_ROWS = 3
FIRST_LINES = 200
LINE_CAP = 300
NARROW_ABOVE = 50
MIN_ONE_TURN = 0.8
ROW = re.compile(r"^  ([^,\n]+),(\d+),(\d+),")
BARE = str.maketrans("", "", '"\\')
TOOLS = ("monokl", "monokl+read", "rg-policy", "rg-early")
SETS = ("identifiers", "questions", "members", "rust", "held-out questions", "held-out members", "held-out rust",
        "report-only", "all")


def tokens(byte_count):
    return math.ceil(byte_count / 3)


def percentile(values, share):
    """Nearest rank: the smallest value with at least `share` of the values at or below it."""
    ordered = sorted(values)
    return ordered[max(math.ceil(share * len(ordered)) - 1, 0)]


def median(values):
    ordered = sorted(values)
    mid = len(ordered) // 2
    return ordered[mid] if len(ordered) % 2 else (ordered[mid - 1] + ordered[mid]) / 2


def rg_lines(path, lang, pattern, extra=()):
    """Non-test `file:line:text` lines of one `rg -n` call, sorted by path so the first lines are stable."""
    args = ["rg", "-n", "--no-heading", "--color", "never", "--sort", "path", *extra]
    for glob in lang.globs:
        args += ["--glob", glob]
    out = RC.run([*args, "-e", pattern, "."], cwd=path, check=False).stdout
    lines = [line.removeprefix("./") for line in out.splitlines()]
    return [line for line in lines if not RC.is_test_path(line.split(":", 1)[0], lang)]


def read_cost(lines):
    """Bytes of the first lines an agent reads from one call, each cut at the cap, with its newline."""
    shown = [line[:LINE_CAP] for line in lines[:FIRST_LINES]]
    return shown, sum(len(line.encode()) + 1 for line in shown)


def word_lines(path, lang, word, cache):
    key = (str(path), word)
    if key not in cache:
        cache[key] = rg_lines(path, lang, re.escape(word), ["-S", "-w"])
    return cache[key]


def best_words(path, lang, words, cache):
    """The words that match at least once, most selective first."""
    counted = [(len(word_lines(path, lang, word, cache)), word) for word in words]
    return [word for count, word in sorted(counted, key=lambda c: (c[0], -len(c[1]), c[1])) if count]


def declaration_lines(path, lang, file, symbol, member):
    """(line number, text) of every declaration of `symbol` in `file`, as rg finds them."""
    pattern = RC.declaration_pattern(symbol, lang, member)
    out = RC.run(["rg", "-n", "--no-heading", "--color", "never", "-e", pattern, file], cwd=path, check=False).stdout
    found = []
    for line in out.splitlines():
        number, _, text = line.partition(":")
        found.append((int(number), text))
    return found


def monokl_spans(binary, symbol, path, file):
    """(first line, last line) of every block monokl returns for `file` when it searches `symbol` with the lean cut
    off (no score floor, no row cap, no token cap). Only extents are read: the declaration is found by rg, and monokl's
    ranking does not choose it."""
    out = RC.run([binary, "search", symbol, ".", "--min-score", "0", "--max-results", "1000000", "--max-tokens",
                  "1000000000", "--snippet-lines", "0"], cwd=path, check=False).stdout
    rows = [(m.group(1).removeprefix("./"), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3)))
            for line in out.splitlines() if (m := ROW.match(line))]
    return sorted({(start, end) for name, start, end in rows if name == file})


def declared_block(spans, declarations):
    """(first line, last line) of the block that is the declaration: for each declaration line, the innermost block
    that holds it (a class that holds a method does not stand in for the method), then the largest of those, so an
    implementation is read in place of its overload signatures. None when no block holds any declaration line."""
    innermost = set()
    for number, _text in declarations:
        holding = [(start, end) for start, end in spans if start <= number <= end]
        if holding:
            innermost.add(min(holding, key=lambda span: (span[1] - span[0], -span[0])))
    return max(innermost, key=lambda span: (span[1] - span[0], -span[0]), default=None)


def span_bytes(lines, span):
    """Bytes of the lines `span` covers (1-based, inclusive), each with its newline."""
    return sum(len(line.encode()) + 1 for line in lines[span[0] - 1:span[1]])


def read_block_bytes(binary, path, expected, symbol, gaps):
    """Bytes of the smallest file read that shows the expected declaration: per expected file the block of
    `declared_block`, then the smallest file. monokl makes no block for a declaration that has no body, such as Rust's
    `mod name;`; that declaration is read as its own line, and each such file is appended to `gaps` so the report
    counts them."""
    sizes = []
    for file, declarations in expected.items():
        lines = (path / file).read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()
        span = declared_block(monokl_spans(binary, symbol, path, file), declarations)
        if span is None:
            gaps.append(f"{path.name}:{file}:{declarations[0][0]}")
            span = (declarations[0][0], declarations[0][0])
        sizes.append(span_bytes(lines, span))
    return min(sizes)


def declaration_prefix(text):
    """The first 40 characters of a declaration line without its export keywords, as rg-compare compares them."""
    bare = re.sub(r"^(?:export\s+|default\s+|declare\s+)+", "", text).rstrip(" {;").strip()
    return bare[:40].translate(BARE)


def monokl_cost(binary, query, path, expected):
    """Runs monokl once; returns (bytes, answerable in the first rows, how many rows were printed)."""
    out = RC.run([binary, "search", query, "."], cwd=path, check=False).stdout
    rows = [(m.group(1).removeprefix("./"), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3)), line)
            for line in out.splitlines() if (m := ROW.match(line))]
    answerable = False
    for file, start, end, text in rows[:TOP_ROWS]:
        shown = text.translate(BARE)
        if file in expected and any(
                start <= number <= end and declaration_prefix(decl) in shown for number, decl in expected[file]):
            answerable = True
    return len(out.encode()), answerable, len(rows)


def rg_policy(path, lang, words, identifier, expected, cache, read):
    """Simulates the rg-only agent; returns its turns, bytes, whether the expected file was read, and the early-stop
    turns and bytes."""
    usable = best_words(path, lang, words, cache)
    turns = []
    if usable:
        first = word_lines(path, lang, usable[0], cache)
        turns.append(first)
        if len(first) > NARROW_ABOVE:
            if identifier:
                narrower = rg_lines(path, lang, RC.declaration_pattern(identifier, lang))
            elif len(usable) > 1:
                a, b = (re.escape(w) for w in usable[:2])
                narrower = rg_lines(path, lang, rf"\b{a}\b.*\b{b}\b|\b{b}\b.*\b{a}\b", ["-i"])
            else:
                narrower = None
            if narrower is not None:
                turns.append(narrower)
    spent = 0
    early = None
    located = False
    for number, lines in enumerate(turns, 1):
        shown, cost = read_cost(lines)
        spent += cost
        for line in shown:
            file, _, rest = line.partition(":")
            if file in expected:
                located = True
                if early is None and int(rest.partition(":")[0]) in {n for n, _ in expected[file]}:
                    early = (number, spent)
    full = (len(turns) + 1, spent + read)
    return full, located, early or full


def identifier_rows(binary, repo_filter, count):
    for name, url, sha, lang, held_out in RC.repositories(repo_filter):
        if held_out:
            continue
        path = RC.checkout(name, url, sha)
        for term in RC.sample_terms(path, count, lang):
            files, _ = RC.split(RC.definitions(term, path, lang), lang)
            if files:
                yield {"repo": name, "lang": lang, "path": path, "kind": "identifier", "query": term,
                       "words": [term], "identifier": term, "symbol": term, "member": False,
                       "files": sorted(files)}


def question_rows(repo_filter):
    checkouts = {name: (RC.checkout(name, url, sha), lang) for name, url, sha, lang, _ in RC.repositories(repo_filter)}
    for repo, words, file, symbol, member, held_out in RC.question_rows(repo_filter):
        path, lang = checkouts[repo]
        yield {"repo": repo, "lang": lang, "path": path, "kind": "member" if member else "question", "query": words,
               "words": words.split(), "identifier": None, "symbol": symbol, "member": member, "files": [file],
               "held_out": held_out}


def set_names(row, report_only):
    rust = row["lang"] is RC.LANGS["rust"]
    held = row.get("held_out", False)
    if held and row["repo"] in report_only:
        name = "report-only"
    elif held:
        name = "held-out rust" if rust else "held-out members" if row["member"] else "held-out questions"
    elif rust:
        name = "rust"
    else:
        name = {"identifier": "identifiers", "question": "questions", "member": "members"}[row["kind"]]
    return [name, "all"]


def score(binary, row, cache, gaps):
    path, lang = row["path"], row["lang"]
    expected = {}
    for file in row["files"]:
        found = declaration_lines(path, lang, file, row["symbol"], row["member"])
        if found:
            expected[file] = found
    if not expected:
        sys.exit(f"{row['repo']}: `{row['symbol']}` has no declaration in {row['files']}; run `just rg-compare`")
    monokl_bytes, answerable, printed = monokl_cost(binary, row["query"], path, expected)
    block = read_block_bytes(binary, path, expected, row["symbol"], gaps)
    (rg_turns, rg_bytes), located, (early_turns, early_bytes) = rg_policy(
        path, lang, row["words"], row["identifier"], expected, cache, block)
    return {
        "repo": row["repo"], "kind": row["kind"], "query": row["query"], "symbol": row["symbol"],
        "expected": sorted(expected), "read": block,
        "answerable": answerable, "rg_located": located, "monokl_rows": printed,
        "monokl": (1, monokl_bytes),
        "monokl+read": (1 if answerable else 2, monokl_bytes + (0 if answerable else block)),
        "rg-policy": (rg_turns, rg_bytes),
        "rg-early": (early_turns, early_bytes),
    }


def table(results, detail):
    print(f"{'set':<19} {'n':>3} {'tool':<11} {'turns med/total':>15} {'bytes median':>13} {'p90':>8} {'total':>10} "
          f"{'tokens median':>14} {'p90':>7} {'total':>9}  answered")
    failures = []
    for name in SETS:
        rows = [r for r in results if name in r["sets"]]
        if not rows:
            continue
        stats = {}
        for tool in TOOLS:
            turns = [r[tool][0] for r in rows]
            sizes = [r[tool][1] for r in rows]
            stats[tool] = median(sizes)
            answered = {"monokl": "answerable in one turn", "rg-policy": "rg located the file"}.get(tool)
            count = sum(r["answerable" if tool == "monokl" else "rg_located"] for r in rows)
            print(f"{name if tool == 'monokl' else '':<19} {len(rows) if tool == 'monokl' else '':>3} {tool:<11} "
                  f"{f'{median(turns):g}/{sum(turns)}':>15} {median(sizes):>13,.0f} {percentile(sizes, 0.9):>8,} "
                  f"{sum(sizes):>10,} {tokens(median(sizes)):>14,} {tokens(percentile(sizes, 0.9)):>7,} "
                  f"{tokens(sum(sizes)):>9,}  "
                  f"{f'{count}/{len(rows)} = {count / len(rows):.0%} {answered}' if answered else ''}")
        rate = sum(r["answerable"] for r in rows) / len(rows)
        if stats["monokl"] > stats["rg-policy"]:
            failures.append(f"{name}: monokl median {stats['monokl']:,.0f} bytes exceeds rg-policy median "
                            f"{stats['rg-policy']:,.0f}")
        if rate < MIN_ONE_TURN:
            failures.append(f"{name}: answerable in one turn {rate:.0%} is below {MIN_ONE_TURN:.0%}")
    if detail:
        print()
        print("per question: repo | kind | query -> symbol | monokl bytes answerable | rg-policy turns bytes located | "
              "rg-early turns bytes")
        for r in results:
            print(f"{r['repo']} | {r['kind']} | {r['query']!r} -> {r['symbol']} | {r['monokl'][1]} "
                  f"{'yes' if r['answerable'] else 'no'} | {r['rg-policy'][0]} {r['rg-policy'][1]} "
                  f"{'yes' if r['rg_located'] else 'no'} | {r['rg-early'][0]} {r['rg-early'][1]}")
    print()
    for failure in failures:
        print(f"FAIL (report-only, exit status unchanged) {failure}")
    return failures


def summary(results, failures):
    rows = results
    monokl = median([r["monokl"][1] for r in rows])
    rg = median([r["rg-policy"][1] for r in rows])
    one_turn = sum(r["answerable"] for r in rows)
    located = sum(r["rg_located"] for r in rows)
    print(f"summary: {len(rows)} questions; median bytes monokl {monokl:,.0f} ({tokens(monokl):,} tokens, 1 turn) vs "
          f"rg-policy {rg:,.0f} ({tokens(rg):,} tokens, {median([r['rg-policy'][0] for r in rows]):g} turns); "
          f"monokl answerable in one turn {one_turn}/{len(rows)} = {one_turn / len(rows):.0%}; "
          f"rg-policy located the file {located}/{len(rows)}; "
          f"{'FAIL x' + str(len(failures)) if failures else 'no failing marker'} (report-only)")


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("--binary", default=str(ROOT / "target" / "release" / "monokl"))
    parser.add_argument("--repo", action="append", help="limit to a repository name from rg-compare.repos")
    parser.add_argument("--terms", type=int, default=25, help="identifiers sampled per repository, as rg-compare.py")
    parser.add_argument("--detail", action="store_true", help="print one line per question after the table")
    parser.add_argument("--json", help="write every row to this path")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    if not Path(args.binary).exists():
        sys.exit(f"{args.binary} not found; run `cargo build --release` or pass --binary")
    RC.configure(args.binary)
    report_only = RC.report_only_repositories()

    cache = {}
    gaps = []
    results = []
    for row in [*identifier_rows(args.binary, args.repo, args.terms), *question_rows(args.repo)]:
        result = score(args.binary, row, cache, gaps)
        result["sets"] = set_names(row, report_only)
        results.append(result)
    if not results:
        sys.exit("no rows to score")

    print("agent workflow cost: one monokl search vs a fixed rg policy; bytes, tokens = ceil(bytes / 3), no timing")
    failures = table(results, args.detail)
    print(f"read sized from monokl's block extents; {len(gaps)} declaration(s) have no block and are read as their own "
          f"line: {', '.join(gaps) or 'none'}")
    summary(results, failures)
    if args.json:
        Path(args.json).write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2, default=str))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

## 46. The default output is lean: one snippet line and a relevance cut (2026-11-15)

- **Decision.** `monokl search` prints, by default, the rows whose `finalScore` is at least 0.3 times the top row's (`--min-score`, 0 turns it off), always the first 8 rows when that many exist, at most 20 (`--max-results`, was 50; the cap wins over the floor), and one snippet line per row (`--snippet-lines`, 0 to 3, was a fixed 3; the lines past the shown ones are still counted). The help line names the flag for each rule that cut rows: `showing 9 of 37; --min-score 0 or --max-results N for more, or refine with +term/-term`. `--snippet-lines 0` is allowed and documented as losing the declaration text of variable and type rows, which have no signature. The old output is `--min-score 0 --max-results 50 --snippet-lines 3`, checked to match the previous output byte for byte on the fixture. No `--offset`: rows past the cap are reached by a narrower query or `--max-results`, a known gap.
- **Why.** An output-economics sweep of the 222 harness rows (the rows of `just rg-compare`, as an agent runs them with default flags) found a median default output of 10 KB, 91% of the bytes in rows past rank 3, an answer in those rows for only 6% of the questions, the snippet half of every row, and 58% of the bytes past rank 3 repeating a file already shown.
- **First choice and why it moved.** The sweep's rule (fraction 0.3, floor 3, cap 15) lost two harness questions against the baseline, which a gate would have hidden: zod `registry add schema` (member `add`: its row is rank 18 of the old output, scoring 10.75 against a top of 23.21, so 46% of the top: the fraction keeps it and the cap of 15 dropped it) and the fd identifier `patterns` (declared by `mod patterns;` in `src/main.rs`, whose first row is rank 6 at 0.082 against a top of 0.384, 21%: the fraction drops it and the floor of 3 did not reach it). The gates stay at 0.9; the parameters moved instead.
- **Chosen from a grid.** Floor in {3, 5, 8}, fraction in {0.15, 0.2, 0.3} and cap in {15, 20}, 18 settings, each scored over the whole harness (`just rg-compare` rows and `scripts/agent-cost.py`) with the cut applied to one cached ranked output per query. A setting qualifies when no harness set is below its baseline (59/59, 17/18, 15/16, Rust 22/24, held-out 32/33 and 22/22, held-out Rust 34/36, react-hook-form 14/14). Seven settings qualify, all with cap 20; all nine cap-15 settings lose the zod member. Of the qualifying settings the smallest total output is floor 8, fraction 0.3, cap 20:

  | floor | fraction | cap | total bytes (222 rows) | median | p90 | qualifies |
  | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
  | 3 | 0.3 | 15 | 318,736 | 920 | 3,207 | no: members 14/16, Rust 21/24 |
  | 5 | 0.3 | 15 | 340,835 | 1,149 | 3,207 | no: members 14/16, Rust 21/24 |
  | 3 | 0.3 | 20 | 358,657 | 920 | 3,993 | no: Rust 21/24 |
  | 3 | 0.2 | 15 | 373,260 | 1,147 | 3,338 | no: members 14/16 |
  | 5 | 0.3 | 20 | 380,756 | 1,149 | 3,993 | no: Rust 21/24 |
- **Rejected.** A cursor or session token: it needs state. Counting the offset before the relevance cut: the cut would then move with the page and a row's inclusion would depend on which page asked for it.

- **Left open.** No `--offset`. The fraction, the floor and the cap are not tuned per language or per query shape. Two `FAIL` lines of `scripts/agent-cost.py` remain, down from nine (§45, whose rg-policy reads were corrected after this was written): `questions` is answerable in one turn on 78% (unchanged), and monokl's median bytes still exceed the rg policy's on Rust (1,442 against 731).

## 48. A Rust row shows a code line and no where clause (2026-11-15)

- **Decision.** Three output-layer changes, no change to what is searched, ranked or counted. (1) The snippet picks code lines before comment and attribute lines: a matched line starting with `//`, `/*`, `*/`, `* `, `#[` or `#![`, and a line inside a Rust where clause, is shown only when fewer than `--snippet-lines` code lines matched or it is the only match; the chosen lines keep block order. TypeScript and Rust share the rule (a JSDoc line or a `// ...` in a body is demoted the same way). (2) A Rust row's `symbolSignature` ends before its `where` clause and says `where …`; the lines of the clause after the declaration line become snippet candidates, because the column no longer shows them. The analyzer's `symbol_signature` and `signature_span` are unchanged (a new field, `where_start`, carries the clause), so ranking (which tokenizes the signature) and the span invariants are unchanged. The analyzer records where the clause starts, from the syntax tree's `WHERE_CLAUSE` node, in a new field `CodeBlock::where_start` (`None` for TypeScript); the output layer cuts at that offset and scans no text for the keyword. Two review findings came from a text scan that did not: `pub fn value() /* where values originate */ -> u64` and a raw string holding `where` in a const-generic default each have no clause. The comment-line check of the snippet is a line-prefix test that only orders lines, so it is not exact and does not need to be: a line wrongly taken for a comment is shown after the other matched lines, never dropped. (3) The count of lines past the snippet reads `+N more` (was `...and N more matching lines`, `...and 1 more matching line`).
- **Why.** The lean default of §46 left the fd Rust median at 1,442 bytes (1,463 after §50) against 731 for the rg policy. The 60 Rust queries of fd, tokio and axum (the sampled identifiers, questions and members; 724 rows, 150,137 bytes) put the bytes here: path 14%, signature 32%, snippet 35%, parent 5%, finalScore 5%, the other columns 9%. 554 rows had a snippet; the first line of 329 of them (59%) was a doc comment (296) or an attribute (33), and 446 rows ended with the `...and N more matching lines` marker, 13,417 bytes (9% of the output). 109 signatures carried a where clause, 5,751 bytes; an `impl` row's clause is often longer than the rest of its signature.

  - *Snippet line that repeats the signature.* None can: a line whose text lies inside `signature_span` is already left out.

## 49. A matching file is opened once, and a parallel walk is not worth it yet (2026-11-15)

Trail 362, after the search sink work. The profile came first, on a machine at load 30 to 40 on 18 cores, so every number is a minimum over alternating runs of the old and new binaries, not a quiet-machine figure.

- **Profile.** `stress/many` (20,000 small matching files, wall ms, min of 12): walk 40, text search 226, analysis 145, rank and dedup 10. `zod` broad: walk 3, search 3, analysis 6, rank 3. `zod` no-match: walk 4, search 4. Analysis opened every surviving file a second time (a size lookup, an open and a read), and on small files that is most of its cost.
- **Decision.** Text search reads a matching file of at most 256 KiB whole, with one read of its known size, and searches the bytes in memory. When the file matches and a shared 16 MiB budget has room, the bytes go to analysis, which uses them instead of looking the file up and opening it again. Anything else is streamed as before and opened again by analysis. The budget changes cost, never output: a test runs the same tree with the budget at zero and full and asserts the same rows and diagnostics. The budget is charged each buffer's capacity (a `KeptText` is the only way to hold text against it), the read never passes the size found when the file was opened, and a buffer from a file that shrank is cut to what was read; a review found the first version charged lengths, so truncated buffers kept their larger allocations unaccounted. The bound is stated in ADR 0004 under rule 2.
- **Measured.** `stress/many` 490 to 359 ms (min of 15 alternating runs, 0.73 of the old time; p50 0.73). `zod` broad 24.1 to 24.4 ms and `zod` no-match 10.4 to 10.7 ms: no change beyond noise, because they open a few hundred files. Output of 96 queries over the five pinned repositories and the stress set is byte-identical to the old binary, and `just rg-compare` scores are unchanged.
- **Counted test.** A search opens each matching file once, at 250 and 1,000 files (opens by text search plus reads by analysis equal the file count and the second is zero); with no budget each file is opened twice; with a budget for 16 of 40 files, 24 are opened again. A reader that gives fewer bytes than the size asked gives a cut buffer; a reader with more gives exactly the size asked; and 300 buffers of 100,000 bytes of capacity holding one byte each keep exactly as many as fit 16 MiB by capacity.

---
monokl: minor
---

**A Rust row costs fewer bytes.** On the 222 rows of the harness the total output falls from 420,764 to 383,506 bytes (8.9%). The fd Rust median falls from 1,463 to 1,322 bytes (p90 3,140 to 2,696) and the held-out Rust median from 3,258 to 2,792 (p90 4,709 to 4,058). Every harness score and every one-turn answer count stays at its baseline.

- **Snippet.** A matched code line is shown before a comment or attribute line: a line starting with `//`, `/*`, `*/`, `* `, `#[` or `#![` (a Rust doc comment, an attribute, a JSDoc line, a comment in a body) is shown only when too few code lines matched or it is the only match. 59% of the Rust rows with a snippet showed a doc comment or an attribute. The shown lines keep their order in the block. TypeScript follows the same rule.
- **Rust signature.** `symbolSignature` ends before the `where` clause and says `where …` in its place, so `impl<L, M, S, F> Debug for WithGracefulShutdown<L, M, S, F> where L: Debug + 'static, M: Debug, ...` becomes `impl<L, M, S, F> Debug for WithGracefulShutdown<L, M, S, F> where …`. A line of the clause that matched is a snippet line, after the code lines. The cut is where the analyzer's syntax tree puts the clause, so a `where` in a comment or a string is not one. Ranking still reads the whole signature.
- **More lines marker.** The count of snippet lines past the shown ones reads `+3 more` (was `...and 3 more matching lines`).
- **Not changed, with the numbers.** No signature starts with an attribute or a doc comment already. The `parent` column is `kind name` and costs 5% of the bytes. Test-path rows are 1.4% of the rows. Capping the signature length and rounding `finalScore` were measured and not taken (docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md, section 48).
- **Still above the rg policy.** The fd Rust median is 1,322 bytes against 731. What remains is the floor of 8 rows.

**Breaking:** `CodeBlock` has a new public field, `where_start`, the offset of the `where` keyword of a Rust declaration's where clause (`None` when there is none, and for TypeScript and JavaScript); code that builds a `CodeBlock` must set it. The text of a row changed. A Rust row's `symbolSignature` drops the where clause and ends in ` where …`; the snippet line is a code line where one matched, and for a Rust item a where-clause line can now be a snippet line; the marker is `+N more` instead of `...and N more matching line(s)`.

**Action:** Set `where_start: None` where you build a `CodeBlock`. Code that parses the marker, or reads a bound out of a Rust `symbolSignature`, must change: the marker is `+N more`, and a where clause is in the file at `lineStart`–`lineEnd`. `search_row_texts` and `render_search` keep their signatures. There is no flag for the old rows.

pub where_start: Option<usize>,
    pub matched_lines: Vec<usize>,
    pub parent: Option<ParentContext>,
}

pub struct RankedBlock {
    pub block: CodeBlock,
    pub final_score: f64,
    pub rank: usize,
}

## Ranking (`rank/`)

```rust
pub fn rank_blocks(blocks: Vec<(CodeBlock, Vec<String>)>, query_terms: &[&str], df: &HashMap<...>)
    -> Vec<RankedBlock>
```

Per block: `bm25 = bm25::score(...)`,
`ntype = boost::node_type_boost(block.node_kind)`, `name = boost::name_match_boost(&block, query_terms)`
(1.0 to 7.0, below), **`final_score = round6(bm25 * name * ntype)`**.
Sorted by `final_score` descending, then file, `line_start`, `line_end`, `node_kind` and `code`; 1-based `rank` is
assigned after the sort.

Both read the byte spans the analyzers fill ([ADR 0005](../adr/0005-hits-and-blocks-are-identified-by-byte-spans-and-blocks-form-a-tree.md)); neither reads line numbers or compares text.

`dedup_blocks` (`dedup.rs`) walks the ranked blocks best first and drops a block that shares more than half of the smaller span's bytes with a block already kept in the same file, then renumbers `rank`. The spans of one analyzed file nest or are disjoint, so this drops a block inside a kept block, equal to it, or holding it, and keeps two blocks that share a line but no byte (`const a = 1; const b = 2;`). A member (a block with a `parent`) never duplicates the top-level block that strictly encloses it, in either rank order. A block with an empty span overlaps nothing. A segment tree over the kept spans' ends keeps the walk near-linear (`tests/scaling.rs`).

The snippet (`output/agent.rs`) shows the matched lines of a block, at most `--snippet-lines` (default 1, up to 3), each cut to 160 characters, with the rest counted (`+2 more`). A matched line is left out when its text lies wholly inside the block's `signature_span`, because the signature column already shows it, except that the signature column of a Rust item ends before its `where` clause (`pub fn f<T>(x: T) -> T where …`, cut by `output/agent.rs` at `CodeBlock.where_start`, which the Rust analyzer takes from the syntax tree; ranking still reads the whole signature), so the lines of the clause after the declaration line are candidates. The shown lines are chosen code lines first: a line that starts with `//`, `/*`, `*/`, `* `, `#[` or `#![` (a doc comment, a block comment, an attribute) or a line inside a where clause comes after every other matched line, so such a line is shown only when too few code lines matched or it is the only match. The chosen lines keep their order in the block, and the ones not chosen are counted. With `--snippet-lines 0` the column is `null`, so a variable or type alias row, which has no signature, shows no declaration text.

## Which rows are printed

`budget.rs` cuts the ranked, deduplicated list in three steps, in this order. Core holds none of them; it returns every ranked block.

1. **Relevance cut** (`--min-score`, default 0.3). Keep the leading rows whose `final_score` is at least `min_score * top`, where `top` is the first row's score. The scores fall down the list, so the kept rows are a prefix. A score equal to the threshold is kept, so rows that tie with the top survive `--min-score 1`. A top score of 0 keeps every row (the threshold is 0). `--min-score 0` turns the cut off.
2. **Floor.** The first eight rows are kept whatever their score, or all of them when there are fewer. The floor lifts the relevance cut only.
3. **Offset** (`--offset`, default 0). Skips that many of the rows the cut kept. The cut is measured against the top row of the whole result, so it is the same whatever the offset, and a page is a slice of one deterministic ranking: pages laid end to end equal one large run. Search stays stateless (ADR 0004): every call re-runs the search, and the offset is the only cursor.
4. **Row cap** (`--max-results`, default 20). Applies to the page and wins over the floor: `--max-results 1` prints one row.
5. **Token cap** (`--max-tokens`, default 20,000). The longest prefix of the page whose printed rows fit; a row larger than the whole cap leaves no rows. It counts the printed rows, so it sees the snippet length, and it does not count the skipped rows.

When any rule dropped rows, or the page starts after the first row, the response is truncated: `totalCount` is the number of ranked blocks and the help line is michi's `showing {returned} of {total}; {guidance}`. The guidance names `next: --offset N` while kept rows remain after the page (`N` is the offset plus the rows returned), `--min-score 0 for the N rows below the cut` when the cut dropped rows (the same offsets still apply with the cut off). `totalCount` and the `of T` in the line count every match, including the N rows below the cut, so the rows reachable by `--offset` alone are `T - N`; `next:` appears only while some of them remain, so following it never reaches an empty page, and `refine with +term/-term`. An empty page that the caps caused names `--max-results N` or `--max-tokens N` instead, because an offset cannot move past a row that does not fit. An offset at or past the last kept row prints no rows, keeps `totalCount`, exits 0 and says `offset 40 is past the last of 31 rows`. The wording is the output layer's (`truncation_guidance`); core carries `total_blocks_before_truncation`, `blocks_cut_by_relevance` and `offset` only.

Why these defaults: [05 §46](../spec/05-research-and-decisions.md). To get the output of versions before the change, run `--min-score 0 --max-results 50 --snippet-lines 3`.

import json
import math

try:
    import tiktoken
    enc = tiktoken.get_encoding("o200k_base")
except Exception:  # noqa
    enc = None

before = json.load(open("target/before.json"))
after = json.load(open("target/after.json"))
assert len(before) == len(after) == 222


def pct(values, share):
    ordered = sorted(values)
    return ordered[max(math.ceil(share * len(ordered)) - 1, 0)]


def med(values):
    ordered = sorted(values)
    mid = len(ordered) // 2
    return ordered[mid] if len(ordered) % 2 else (ordered[mid - 1] + ordered[mid]) / 2


for label, rows in (("before", before), ("after", after)):
    b = [r["monokl"][1] for r in rows]
    t = [math.ceil(x / 3.5) for x in b]
    print(label, "bytes median", med(b), "p90", pct(b, 0.9), "total", sum(b),
          "| tokens(bytes/3.5) median", med(t), "p90", pct(t, 0.9), "total", sum(t),
          "| answerable", sum(r["answerable"] for r in rows), "tiktoken" if enc else "no tiktoken")
tb = sum(r["monokl"][1] for r in before)
ta = sum(r["monokl"][1] for r in after)
print("total change", f"{(ta - tb) / tb:+.1%}")
for name in ("identifiers", "questions", "members", "rust", "held-out questions", "held-out members", "held-out rust", "report-only", "all"):
    bs = [r["monokl"][1] for r in before if name in r["sets"]]
    as_ = [r["monokl"][1] for r in after if name in r["sets"]]
    ab = sum(r["answerable"] for r in before if name in r["sets"])
    aa = sum(r["answerable"] for r in after if name in r["sets"])
    print(f"| {name} | {len(bs)} | {med(bs):,.0f} | {med(as_):,.0f} | {pct(bs, .9):,} | {pct(as_, .9):,} | {ab} / {aa} |")

cat >> docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md <<'EOF'

## 51. A search row ends in `relevance`, not `rank` and `finalScore` (2026-11-16)

- **Decision.** The row columns are `file,lineStart,lineEnd,nodeKind,parent,symbolSignature,snippet,relevance`. `rank` is gone. `finalScore` is replaced by `relevance`: the row's score as an integer percent of the top row's score (top row 100, rounded to the nearest whole number, clamped to 0..=100). The float score stays in core for the sort and the relevance cut; `SearchResponse::top_score` carries the best score of the whole ranking, so a page after `--offset` still measures against the first row of the result. The output layer computes the percent from `final_score` and `top_score`, the floats the sort and the cut use, never from printed text. A top score that is not positive leaves nothing to divide by; every row then ties with the top under the cut (the threshold is 0), so each shows 100. No other column, no order and no lean default changed.
- **Name.** `relevance`: columns are camelCase words (`lineStart`, `symbolSignature`, `nodeKind`), and one lower-case word fits that; `scorePct` would have named the unit instead of the meaning and nothing in michi's field handling needed it. The `--min-score` help, the README and the paging hint use the same word: the hint says `--min-score 0 for the 2 rows below relevance 30`, where 30 is 100 times `--min-score` (rounded to a whole number).
- **It lines up with the cut.** The cut keeps a row with `score >= min_score * top`, so a kept row shows at least `100 * min_score` and the rows the cut dropped show less. Two exceptions, both stated in the docs: the first 8 rows are kept whatever their score, so a printed row can be under the line, and a row within half a point below the line rounds up onto it.
- **Why.** A column-economics study of the 222 harness queries (2,038 rows, `o200k_base` tokens) found:
  - `rank` equals the row index in 2,038 of 2,038 rows and is 3.8% of the tokens. A reader has the position already. Nothing in `scripts/rg-compare.py` or `scripts/agent-cost.py` reads it.
  - `finalScore` is 9.2% of the tokens, as 6-decimal floats, and nothing in the scripts reads it. The ratio of the top two scores is informative (AUC 0.80 for telling whether the first row is the answer; a ratio of 1.5 or more flags 118 queries as clear, with 94% precision) but absolute scores are not comparable across queries (BM25 depends on the corpus). So the score is kept as a share of the top row, which carries the ratio and drops the digits.
- **Rejected.**
  - *Merge `lineStart` and `lineEnd` into one `lines` cell.* Saves tokens but breaks `scripts/agent-cost.py`, whose row pattern needs `file,lineStart,lineEnd` first: one-turn answerable falls from 206 to 0. It would also change the shape every reader parses.
  - *`lineStart` plus a span length.* Same break, and a reader has to add to get the end line.
  - *A short `nodeKind`.* Saves a few bytes a row and costs a lookup; the full words are the ones a model already knows.
  - *Blank repeated files.* A row that repeats the file above it leaves the cell empty. Rows are read one at a time and a reader that sees an empty cell cannot tell it from a missing value.
  - *Group by file.* Prints each file once with its rows below it. It reorders the rows: 136 of 222 queries would not keep the ranking's order, and the order is the answer to which block is best.
  - *`null` as an empty cell.* The columns use `null` to say "none" (`parent`, `snippet`), and an empty cell would read as an empty string, which a snippet or a signature can be.
  - *Score at 1 or 2 decimals.* One decimal makes the top two rows tie in 7 queries, which loses exactly the ratio the study found informative; two decimals still cost the digits and the cross-query comparison the digits invite.
  - *Drop `finalScore` outright.* Loses the ratio that tells a reader whether the first row stands alone (AUC 0.80) and the link to `--min-score`, which a reader can no longer check against the rows.
- **Measured** (the real binary, `just agent-cost --json`, 222 rows, main at 701adec8 before and this change after; bytes of one `monokl search <words> .`; tokens are bytes / 3.5 because no `o200k_base` tokenizer was available in the sandbox, so the study's token shares above are the study's and the figures below are bytes):

  | set | n | median before | median after | p90 before | p90 after | one turn before / after |
  | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
  | identifiers | 59 | 463 | 432 | 1,518 | 1,440 | 59 / 59 |
  | questions | 18 | 1,717 | 1,640 | 3,089 | 2,918 | 14 / 14 |
  | members | 16 | 1,510 | 1,444 | 4,126 | 3,940 | 14 / 14 |
  | rust (fd) | 24 | 1,322 | 1,255 | 2,696 | 2,567 | 20 / 20 |
  | held-out questions | 33 | 1,581 | 1,509 | 3,703 | 3,525 | 32 / 32 |
  | held-out members | 22 | 1,471 | 1,402 | 2,366 | 2,295 | 22 / 22 |
  | held-out rust | 36 | 2,792 | 2,648 | 4,058 | 3,869 | 32 / 32 |
  | report-only | 14 | 2,108 | 2,022 | 3,690 | 3,516 | 13 / 13 |
  | all | 222 | 1,456 | 1,387 | 3,623 | 3,434 | 206 / 206 |

  The total falls from 383,506 to 365,518 bytes (4.7%); the median at 3.5 bytes a token falls from 417 to 397 tokens and the p90 from 1,036 to 982. This is about half of the 9% the study's token shares suggested: a float's digits cost more tokens per byte than the rest of a row, so bytes understate the saving, but that was not measured here.
- **Harness** (`just rg-compare`): every set equals main's (identifiers 59/59, questions 17/18, members 15/16, Rust fd 22/24, held-out 32/33 and 22/22, held-out Rust 35/36, react-hook-form 14/14), and `scripts/agent-cost.py` answerable in one turn is 206 of 222, as before.
- **Left open.** A reader that wants the raw score has no way to get it. Whether a model uses `relevance` is not measured; the study counted tokens, not behavior.
EOF

  | all | 222 | 1,456 | 1,387 | 3,623 | 3,434 | 206 / 206 |

It compares the rows of one query; a raw score cannot be compared across queries. A page printed with `--offset` measures against the top row of the whole result, so its first row is not 100.
- **It lines up with `--min-score`.** The cut keeps rows scoring at least `--min-score` times the top, so the rows it drops have a `relevance` below 100 times it. The help line says so: `--min-score 0 for the 2 rows below relevance 30`. The first 8 rows are kept whatever their `relevance`.

The paging hint reads `--min-score 0 for the N rows below relevance P`, was `below the cut`.

**Action:** Parse rows by header name, not by position: `rank` is no longer the second to last cell. To rank-order rows, use row order. `relevance` is a percent of the top row, so use it to see how far a row is from the first, not as a score. Code that builds a `SearchResponse` must set `top_score` (`apply_budget` sets it from the ranking), and code that builds a `SearchView` must set `min_score` (`SearchView::default()` carries the default). A search row loses `rank` and its `finalScore` becomes `relevance`: the score as a whole percent of the top row's score (top row 100, nearest integer, clamped to 0..=100).
